notes: Gen 76 + Web 404 — DELETE-STICKINESS-NOV10 (owner ruling, Nov 10, 2026, 10:11: "Do what you have to — no deletes if the cloud and app both agree... If they disagree the option to delete has to be there!"): a DELIBERATE delete of a record-list entry (revenue, fuel, PTI, damage, documents, sessions, revenue extras) now STICKS on every device. Before this, the v241/v272 never-lose union made a delete on one device unreachable to any device still holding the record — and the holder resurrected it into the cloud on its next push (the Nov 10 $695.98 auto revenue entry: deleted in the web session at 08:05, still on the phone at 10:03, its Revenue tile still reading it). THE FIX (js/cloudsync.js + modules/preferences.js): the delete is TOMBSTONED into the record's own cloud document as a sibling del field ({recordId: {t, fp}} — when it was deleted + the agreed record's content fingerprint), written in the same write as the list itself, so a pull can never see the list without its tombstones. A device still holding the record drops it on its next cycle and cannot resurrect it; every holder re-asserts the tombstones it accepted (top-level meta m.dels), so even a rolled-back document cannot undelete. A tombstone is authored ONLY from the agreed shadow (pendingRecordDeletes: an identity in the shadow, absent locally, still in the cloud) — a record that exists only on one device is never tombstoned away, and identities are unique per creation, so a genuinely new record can never collide with a tombstone. DISAGREEMENT (deleted on one side, EDITED on the other after the delete — content fingerprint differs from the agreed one): the tombstone cannot settle it, so the record is held back from the cloud and the choice surfaces on the Preferences > Advanced cloud-sync card — "Deleted on another device, but changed on this phone: <record>. Keep your copy, or delete it here too?" [Delete it] [Keep my copy] (CloudSync.resolveDelConflict; status().delConflicts) — a Keep restores the record everywhere and revokes the tombstone in the doc, a Delete drops it everywhere; conflicts never paint the sync dot. GC RULE: a tombstone is dropped only when older than 90 days AND its id is absent from both the merged list and the cloud list at that moment. Never-lose survives untouched for records nobody deleted (World B below). Bench: tools/delete-stickiness-nov10-test.js (new) — failing-first on live-402 bytes 16 passed / 13 failed, 29/29 here: (A) web deletes the $695.98 shape, the phone drops it on its next cycle and cannot resurrect it across further cycles; (B) rollback world — the union still restores a fill nobody deleted and no tombstone is authored; (C/C2) delete-vs-later-edit — the choice surfaces, the edited copy is held back from the cloud while undecided, Delete drops it everywhere, Keep restores it to the cloud, revokes the tombstone, the deleting device takes it back, no oscillation; (D) a local-only never-agreed record beside a foreign tombstone is untouched and pushes up normally. The cloudsync regression family and the wider sync/preferences sweep stand at pristine web-402 standings (every failure pre-existing and identical).
